hits.video_tip: Cut a 60-120s psychological-horror short: a person slowly losing track of what is real while an AI voice reassures them. Open on the creepiest frame in the first second, no title card, let the two-word caption do the rest.
hits.draft_en:
Sometimes the best caption is the shortest one.

Two words, a strong video, and the audience fills in the rest. Gossip Goblin proved it again with AI Psychosis.

My rule now: if the video needs a paragraph to explain it, the video is not done yet.

virals.name: Zasti
virals.text:
A BUS IS PARKED ON THE EDGE OF A CLIFF. 8M VIEWS. $8,000 IN CLIENT ORDERS.

a yellow excavator digs on a grassy lip of rock, a river and a village far down the valley, mountains going blue in the distance. a long white bus is parked right along the drop, its wheels hidden, the ground under it cut away on one side.

then a man in black, a mask and glasses, kneeling in the empty shell with a drill and a bundle of red and blue wire. frames go up, insulation goes in, wooden panels, a roller of paint, a platform bed with drawers built into it. he carries furniture in. at the end there's a bed with pillows, warm light along the ceiling, plants, a desk with a laptop and a telescope, and a window the size of the wall with the whole mountain range in it.

nobody asks how the bus got there. there's no road, no tracks, and the excavator is digging a hole under its own ground. the video moves too fast to ask.

the clip didn't sell anything. it was the demo. 8M people watched it, and some of them were people who need a video made: brands, small studios, anyone with something to show and no crew. they didn't ask what the author charges. they asked for the same thing, with their product in it.

that's how a single clip turned into $8,000 of orders. the view count brought the audience. the quality of the work brought the clients.

why it works:

→ an impossible place, then a payoff: empty on one side, finished on the other
→ every stage is readable with the sound off
→ the view in the last shot is the thing everyone wants, so people watch to the end to see it
→ one man in black as the anchor, so the story has a hero without a single face
→ a dozen small steps instead of one long scene, and each step is its own short clip

how it's made:

→ 1. plan the stages. Claude or ChatGPT: "list the stages of converting a bus into a studio on a cliff, from digging to the finished room, one visual per stage." you get a shot list.
→ 2. a key frame for every stage. Flux, Midjourney, Grok Imagine or Seedream, with the same wording and the same reference images so the bus, the light and the man look like one set.
→ 3. image to video, one stage per clip. Kling, Runway, Luma Dream Machine, Hailuo or Veo, each clip a few seconds.
→ 4. keep the man consistent: the same reference photo in every generation, the same black clothes, mask and glasses.
→ 5. CapCut or DaVinci: join the clips, speed them up like a timelapse, add a quiet building soundtrack.
→ 6. post with the AI-generated label on.

the exterior prompt:

"Yellow excavator digging on a grassy cliff edge, a long white bus parked along the edge of a steep drop, panoramic mountain valley with a river and a village in the distance, photorealistic, cinematic"

the interior prompt:

"Inside an empty white bus, a man in black clothes and a mask installing electrical wires with a drill, cables on the floor, mountain view through the windows, photorealistic timelapse style"

the finale:

"Luxury modern bus interior conversion, wooden ceiling, tiled floor, bed with pillows, warm LED lighting, desk with laptop and telescope, large windows with a mountain panorama, photorealistic, cinematic"

the first take is never the one you keep. most of the cost is retries.

the bus was the demo. the view was the pitch.

virals.video_tip: Recreate the formula: an impossible location, 10-12 short image-to-video stages with one faceless anchor character, sped up like a timelapse, and the money shot saved for the last frame.

Impossible location, a dozen short stages, one faceless builder, and the payoff saved for the final shot.

Brands see a clip like that and want their own version of it. That is how views turn into clients.

virals.text: Yeni YouTube videom yayında. Bu videoda başta Seedance 2.5 ve Kling 4.0 olmak üzere en popüler 8 video modelini 3 farklı yöntem üzerinden kıyasladım. İyi seyirler. Link aşağıda 👇
virals.original_en: My new YouTube video is live. In it I compare the 8 most popular video models, led by Seedance 2.5 and Kling 4.0, across 3 different methods. Enjoy. Link below.
virals.hook: Turkish creator: a YouTube comparison of 8 video models, led by Seedance 2.5 and Kling 4.0, across 3 methods.
virals.video_tip: Post a 30-45s split-screen teaser: same prompt, 4 models in a grid, a scorecard overlay, and the long version linked in the reply.
virals.draft_en:
Everyone asks which video model is best. Wrong question.

Seedance 2.5 is great for motion and camera moves. Kling 4.0 holds characters together better. The right pick depends on the shot, not the leaderboard.

Run the same prompt through both before you commit to a scene.

The game’s official subreddit has updated its rules to ban any content created wholly or partly with generative AI.

That includes:

• AI-generated text summaries
• Image edits and AI “art”
• Animated clips and video
outsiders.hook: Gaming news account: a game's official subreddit banned anything made wholly or partly with generative AI.
outsiders.video_tip: Talking-head or screen-record reaction: show the rule text, then a side-by-side of a fully AI clip vs. an AI-assisted edit, and ask where the line should be.
outsiders.draft_en:
A game community banning generative AI content is not the end of AI video. It is a signal.

Audiences are tired of lazy output, not of the tools. The fix is taste: real direction, real editing, a story worth finishing.

Where do you draw the line between AI-assisted and AI-generated?

outsiders.name: Zasti
outsiders.text:
A BUS IS PARKED ON THE EDGE OF A CLIFF. 8M VIEWS. $8,000 IN CLIENT ORDERS.

a yellow excavator digs on a grassy lip of rock, a river and a village far down the valley, mountains going blue in the distance. a long white bus is parked right along the drop, its wheels hidden, the ground under it cut away on one side.

then a man in black, a mask and glasses, kneeling in the empty shell with a drill and a bundle of red and blue wire. frames go up, insulation goes in, wooden panels, a roller of paint, a platform bed with drawers built into it. he carries furniture in. at the end there's a bed with pillows, warm light along the ceiling, plants, a desk with a laptop and a telescope, and a window the size of the wall with the whole mountain range in it.

nobody asks how the bus got there. there's no road, no tracks, and the excavator is digging a hole under its own ground. the video moves too fast to ask.

the clip didn't sell anything. it was the demo. 8M people watched it, and some of them were people who need a video made: brands, small studios, anyone with something to show and no crew. they didn't ask what the author charges. they asked for the same thing, with their product in it.

that's how a single clip turned into $8,000 of orders. the view count brought the audience. the quality of the work brought the clients.

why it works:

→ an impossible place, then a payoff: empty on one side, finished on the other
→ every stage is readable with the sound off
→ the view in the last shot is the thing everyone wants, so people watch to the end to see it
→ one man in black as the anchor, so the story has a hero without a single face
→ a dozen small steps instead of one long scene, and each step is its own short clip

how it's made:

→ 1. plan the stages. Claude or ChatGPT: "list the stages of converting a bus into a studio on a cliff, from digging to the finished room, one visual per stage." you get a shot list.
→ 2. a key frame for every stage. Flux, Midjourney, Grok Imagine or Seedream, with the same wording and the same reference images so the bus, the light and the man look like one set.
→ 3. image to video, one stage per clip. Kling, Runway, Luma Dream Machine, Hailuo or Veo, each clip a few seconds.
→ 4. keep the man consistent: the same reference photo in every generation, the same black clothes, mask and glasses.
→ 5. CapCut or DaVinci: join the clips, speed them up like a timelapse, add a quiet building soundtrack.
→ 6. post with the AI-generated label on.

the exterior prompt:

"Yellow excavator digging on a grassy cliff edge, a long white bus parked along the edge of a steep drop, panoramic mountain valley with a river and a village in the distance, photorealistic, cinematic"

the interior prompt:

"Inside an empty white bus, a man in black clothes and a mask installing electrical wires with a drill, cables on the floor, mountain view through the windows, photorealistic timelapse style"

the finale:

"Luxury modern bus interior conversion, wooden ceiling, tiled floor, bed with pillows, warm LED lighting, desk with laptop and telescope, large windows with a mountain panorama, photorealistic, cinematic"

the first take is never the one you keep. most of the cost is retries.

the bus was the demo. the view was the pitch.

outsiders.video_tip: Recreate the formula: an impossible location, 10-12 short image-to-video stages with one faceless anchor character, sped up like a timelapse, and the money shot saved for the last frame.

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
